description: Port-forward / NAT rules published on the module's behalf.
_note: nat-manager reconciles the rule set — including removing rules that are no longer declared — so this is apply:'reconcile' for the same reason network:rules is: a removal cannot be expressed as a scalar diff.

natRules.description: Destination-NAT (port-forward) mappings that expose an internal service port on the firewall's WAN interface. Each entry is compiled into an OPNsense rdr-pass rule (translate + allow in one rule). Use this for non-HTTP ports (e.g. SSH); use network:proxy for HTTP(S). All rules forward to this module's single target (its 'ip', or <vmname>.<zone0>.internal).

externalPort.description: Port exposed on the firewall WAN interface (e.g. 2022).

internalPort.description: Service port on the target host. Defaults to externalPort when omitted.

description.description: Human-readable purpose of this port-forward (audit/documentation). Combined with the module name to form the rule's identity.

natRules.note: Activated when network:nat is in dependsOn. Rules are created as rdr-pass on the WAN interface, so no separate network:rules ingress entry is needed for the forwarded port.
natRules.changeNote: Each entry publishes an inside service on an outside address/port. A NAT change is a live firewall change: existing connections may reset, but no guest is rebooted, so it needs no disruption authorization.
